newsitem.title: FRANCE: Apple unveils two new products.
newsitem.headline: Apple unveils two new products.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. on Tuesday unveiled two new products -- a portable computer for schoolchildren and a powerful laptop computer -- and denied rumours it had decided to scrap the Pippin multimedia machine and game station.
Asked about Pippin at a news conference, Apple executive Bjoern Gustavsson said, "We have not yet decided. We will honour our commitments to our license holders."
The troubled computer maker is undergoing a major restructuring and speculation is growing over the future of Pippin, including the possibility it might be sold.

Japan's Bandai Co. Ltd., which recently struck an alliance deal with computer game giant Sega Enterprises Ltd., has a license for the Pippin and Katz Media Group Inc. will shortly launch the CD-ROM game player in France.
"I believe that a machine like the Pippin can help get the necessary volumes for CD-ROM publishers to finally make some money," added Gustavsson, a top European executive for Apple.
He unveiled the "eMate" portable computer for schoolchildren, due to be sold for $700 in the United States, with shipping scheduled for March.
The eMate is a sturdy but light computer that uses the platform of the Newton digital assistant. It will be launched in Europe later.
Gustavsson was standing in for Apple Chief Operating Officer Marco Landi, who could not come to Europe due to the Cupertino, Calif.-based computer company's latest restructuring.
Gustavsson also displayed a powerful Powerbook laptop computer code-named "Hooper" and slated for launch next month.

Hooper runs on a 200-megahertz PowerPC computer chip made by Motorola Inc., allowing it to display a realistic video image, which was demonstrated with a little camera mounted on top of the machine and carried around the conference room.
"We broke the 200-megahertz barrier for laptops," Gustavsson said.
Apple also unveiled the sleek "Spartacus" concept -- or prototype -- computer, which marries modern design with high performance and a Bose sound system.
Apple stock was unchanged at $15.625 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
